'''Dame Caroline Dean''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|DBE|FRS}}<ref name=royal>{{cite web |url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo==%27EC%2F2004%2F15%27) |title=EC/2004/15: Dean, Caroline |publisher=The Royal Society |archive-date=10 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190710033835/https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=%28RefNo%3D%3D%27EC%2F2004%2F15%27%29 |location=London }}</ref> (born 2 April 1957) is a British [[Botany|plant scientist]] working at the [[John Innes Centre]].<ref name="New Phytologist-2025">{{Cite journal |date=30 July 2025 |title=Caroline Dean |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q135644104 |journal=New Phytologist |volume=248 |issue=1 |article-number=nph.70423 |doi=10.1111/NPH.70423 |pmid=40739663 |bibcode=2025NewPh.248...50. }}</ref>  She is focused on understanding the molecular controls used by plants to seasonally judge when to flower.<ref name=gs/> She is specifically interested in vernalisation — the acceleration of [[Flower|flowering]] in plants by exposure to periods of prolonged cold.<ref name=pgen>{{cite Q|Q21144889|article-number=e1003593|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="rosetta">{{Cite Q|Q33337109}}</ref><ref name=frigida>{{Cite Q|Q33921320 }}</ref> She has also served on the Life Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] from 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Infosys Prize – Jury 2020|url=http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/jury/jury-2020.asp|access-date=10 December 2020|website=www.infosys-science-foundation.com}}</ref>

==Education==
Dean was educated at the [[University of York]], where she was awarded a Bachelor of Arts degree in [[Biology]] in 1978 and a PhD in Biology<ref name="deanphd"/> in 1982.<ref name="vern">{{cite Q|Q34288707 }}</ref><ref name="jicprofile">{{cite web|url=http://www.jic.ac.uk/profile/caroline-dean.asp |title=Caroline Dean, Cell & Developmental Biology |archive-date=16 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130616011944/http://www.jic.ac.uk/profile/caroline-dean.asp |date=23 November 2018 }}</ref>

==Research and career==
Dean's research has been funded by the [[Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council]] (BBSRC)<ref name="bbsrc">{{cite web |url=http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/person/F2DDB4A0-400A-4441-88F3-5C9389AF6784 |archive-url=https://webarchive.nationalarchives.gov.uk/ukgwa/20130705133243mp_/http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/person/F2DDB4A0%2D400A%2D4441%2D88F3%2D5C9389AF6784 |archive-date=5 July 2013 |title=UK Government Grants awarded to Caroline Dean }}, via [[Research Councils UK]]</ref> [[European Research Council]] (ERC), EU-Marie Curie and [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]] and focuses on research on [[gene regulation]] and the intersection of [[chromatin]], transcription and [[non-coding RNA]]s. Her goal is to understand the chromatin dynamics that enable switching between [[epigenetic]] states and quantitative regulation of gene expression. This mechanistic analysis is focused on one gene encoding the floral repressor [[Flowering Locus C]]: ''FLC''. Epigenetic switching and quantitative regulation of ''FLC'' play a central role in seasonal timing in plants.  This acceleration of flowering by prolonged cold is a classic epigenetic process called [[Vernalization|vernalisation.]]<ref name="rosetta" /><ref name="frigida" />

''FLC'' regulation involves an antisense-mediated chromatin mechanism that coordinately influences transcription initiation and elongation. As plants [[Overwintering|overwinter]], ''FLC'' expression is then epigenetically silenced through a cold-induced, cis-based, [[Polycomb-group proteins|polycomb switching mechanism]]. The group are mechanistically dissecting these conserved chromatin mechanisms and investigating how they have been modulated during adaptation.

She uses ''[[Arabidopsis]]'' as a reference to establish the regulatory hierarchy and then use this information to translate into other species.<ref name="New Phytologist-2025" /> She was a pioneer in ''Arabidopsis'' becoming a key model organism in plant science.<ref name=anint>{{Cite Q|Q47985864}}</ref><ref name="trap">{{Cite Q|Q34300850
|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="recomb">{{Cite Q|Q56774614 }}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Her nomination for the Royal Society reads: {{centered pull quote|Dean has made outstanding contributions in the study of developmental timing in plants. Her work has revealed the mechanism by which plants remember they have experienced winter, demonstrated novel [[RNA]] processing mechanisms controlling flowering and determined the molecular basis of natural variation in Arabidopsis flowering time. Her discoveries have broad significance in the fields of [[epigenetics]], post-transcriptional regulation and [[molecular evolution]]. Dean has also made a massive contribution to the development of Arabidopsis as a model, establishing resources for genetic mapping and insertional mutagenesis, and providing physical maps that underpinned the sequencing of the genome.<ref name=royal/>}} Other awards include:

* 1993 – 2002  Honorary Research Fellow, School of Biological Sciences, [[University of East Anglia]]
* 1999 – Elected a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO)
* 2004 – Appointed [[Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (DBE) 
* 2004 – Elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS)<ref name=whoswho/>
* 2007 – Awarded the [[Genetics Society Medal]] <ref>{{Cite web |title=Genetics Society Medal |url=https://genetics.org.uk/medals-and-prizes/genetics-society-medals-and-lectures/genetics-society-medal/ |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=Genetics Society |language=en-GB}}</ref>
* 2008 – the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] elected her a foreign member<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/caroline-dean-j5tnmm/|title=Caroline Dean|website=nasonline.org|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>
* 2008 – elected a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]{{fact|date=February 2025}}
* 2015 – [[Federation of European Biochemical Societies]] (FEBS)/[[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO) Women in Science Award<ref>{{Cite web |title=Women in Science |url=https://www.febs.org/other-activities/women-in-science/ |website=Federation of European Biochemical Societies |date=4 August 2022 }}</ref>
* 2016 – Appointed [[Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (DBE) in the 2016 Birthday Honours for services to plant science research and women in science.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=61608|supp=y|page=B8|date=11 June 2016}}</ref>
* 2016 – Dean was awarded with the [[Darwin Medal]] by the Royal Society for her work addressing fundamental questions in the perception of temperature cues and how modifications in epigenetic mechanisms play an important role in adaptation.<ref>[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dsunM9ukGLgaW3HdG9cvJ_QKd7pWjGI0qi_fCb1ROD4/pubhtml?gid=216486814&single=true Darwin Medal 2016]</ref>
* 2018 – Awarded the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards|L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Award]]
* 2020 – Received the [[Wolf Prize in Agriculture]].<ref>{{Cite web| title = Caroline Dean| work = Wolf Foundation| access-date = 13 September 2023| date = 13 January 2020| url = https://wolffund.org.il/2020/01/13/caroline-dean| archive-date = 25 January 2020| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200125220533/https://wolffund.org.il/2020/01/13/caroline-dean/| url-status = dead}}</ref>
*2020 – Awarded the [[Royal Medal]] by the [[Royal Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|date=4 August 2020|title=Royal Society award for Professor Dame Caroline Dean|url=https://www.jic.ac.uk/news/royal-society-award-for-professor-dame-caroline-dean/|access-date=20 January 2021|website=John Innes Centre|language=en-GB}}</ref>
*2023 – Awarded the Mendel Medal by [[The Genetics Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mendel Medal 2023 – Professor Dame Caroline Dean |url=https://genetics.org.uk/medals-and-prizes/2023-winners-2/mendel-medal-2023/ |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=The Genetics Society |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dean married to [[Jonathan D. G. Jones]] in 1991 and has one son and one daughter.<ref name="whoswho"/><ref name=genomebiology/>
